## What you should be able to do tonight

- Return a covariance estimate from one function with the estimator selectable, all guaranteed positive definite.
- Show the four estimators' predicted-versus-realised risk on the same rolling out-of-sample test.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write qlib/risk.py with `covariance(returns, method)` supporting sample, clipped, Ledoit-Wolf and single-factor, each returning a positive definite matrix. Add a test asserting positive definiteness and symmetry for every method on every rolling window of your sample.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Produce the comparison figure milestone 4 needs: for each estimator, out-of-sample realised risk of the minimum-variance portfolio against the risk it predicted, with equal weighting marked as the horizontal reference. Save it into reports/milestone-04-risk-model.md.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/risk.py gives the project one covariance interface with four estimators behind it, tested for positive definiteness on every window. The portfolio construction code no longer knows or cares which estimator is in use.
:::
